key_insight: ACADiff uses clinical-aware latent diffusion to synthesize missing brain imaging modalities by progressively denoising latent representations conditioned on available scans and patient metadata, producing clinically coherent imputations with high fidelity.
problem_solved: Addresses the missing-modality problem in multimodal neuroimaging datasets (common in Alzheimer's research) by generating plausible, clinically consistent images for absent modalities so subjects need not be discarded and downstream models can use more complete data.
method: Latent diffusion in a compressed representation to efficiently generate high-quality imaging modalities.
Adaptive conditioning that attends to available imaging modalities and clinical metadata (e.g., age, diagnosis, cognitive scores) during progressive denoising.
Joint training with reconstruction/modality-consistency and clinical-aware losses to ensure realistic and diagnostically relevant imputations.
impact: Provides a practical way for ML practitioners to recover missing medical imaging modalities, improving dataset completeness and robustness of downstream diagnostic models while leveraging clinical context for more reliable syntheses.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: inputs (available scans + clinical metadata) → latent encoder → conditioned diffusion denoising → decoded synthesized modality.
Denoising timeline: sequence of latent-space steps showing coarse-to-fine image refinement.
Before/after image panels: example slices for real vs. imputed modalities annotated with clinical labels.
Performance charts: imputation accuracy, downstream diagnostic metrics (e.g., classification AUC) and ablation results showing impact of clinical conditioning.
paper_title: Adaptive Clinical-Aware Latent Diffusion for Multimodal Brain Image Generation and Missing Modality Imputation
paper_authors: Rong Zhou, Houliang Zhou, Yao Su, Brian Y. Chen, Yu Zhang
